item.title: Florida Tax Watch President Breaks Down Amendment 3 — And Raises a Warning About Fee Increases
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Former Lieutenant Governor Jeff Kottkamp — now President and CEO of Florida Tax Watch — joined Pensacola's Morning News Thursday with guest host Todd Thompson to walk listeners through what Amendment 3 would actually do to local government budgets if Florida voters approve it in November. Kottkamp was careful to…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Former Lieutenant Governor Jeff Kottkamp — now President and CEO of Florida Tax Watch — joined Pensacola's Morning News Thursday with guest host Todd Thompson to walk listeners through what Amendment 3 would actually do to local government budgets if Florida voters approve it in November.


Kottkamp was careful to note upfront that Florida Tax Watch is a nonpartisan independent organization — it does not endorse or oppose the amendment. Its role is to make sure voters understand the facts before they decide.


The Numbers

The amendment raises the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes — currently at $50,000 — in two steps. On January 1st of 2027 it rises to $150,000. That change alone would cost local governments statewide approximately $4.9 billion in lost revenue. On January 1st of 2028 it rises again to $250,000 — an $8.7 billion annual hit to local government revenue. Starting January 1st of 2029 the exemption is indexed for inflation — pushing the total statewide impact to approximately $11.8 billion annually. For Pensacola specifically Kottkamp put the loss at approximately $8.2 million.


The amendment also reduces the annual assessment cap on non-homestead properties — rental homes, commercial buildings, investment properties — from 10 percent to 5 percent annually. That is an additional reduction in property tax revenue beyond the homestead exemption changes.


The Fee Increase Concern

Kottkamp says one of Florida Tax Watch's biggest concerns is that voters may approve the amendment expecting a significant tax cut — only to see local governments offset their losses by raising fees. The amendment does not prohibit local governments from increasing fees to make up the revenue difference. Kottkamp says solid waste fees, stormwater fees, and fire service impact fees are all tools local governments could use to backfill lost property tax revenue. He says if that happens residents would effectively be paying the same amount — just in a different form.


Constrained Counties

Kottkamp also flagged the situation for fiscally constrained counties — roughly 30 counties statewide that can barely afford to operate under current revenue. After the amendment passed the legislature the governor's office created a pool of money to help backfill losses for those counties — but the House did not go along with it and it was stripped from the final bill. Kottkamp says those counties face the most severe consequences if the amendment passes with no replacement mechanism.


What Florida Tax Watch Would Prefer

Kottkamp says Florida has a Taxation and Budget Reform Commission that convenes every 20 years — a panel appointed by the governor, the House speaker, and the Senate president — with a year and a half to two years to study tax policy and put thoughtful proposals on the ballot. He says Florida Tax Watch would much prefer this kind of property tax reform go through that commission rather than being rushed through a three-day special session without full analysis of all the downstream effects.


Florida Tax Watch is releasing a comprehensive Amendment 3 information portal at floridataxwatch.org next Friday — designed to answer every question voters might have before November. The amendment requires 60 percent voter approval to take effect.

item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola Police Department PIO Mike Wood joined Pensacola Morning News Thursday — guest hosted by Greater Pensacola Chamber President Todd Thompson — with a wide-ranging update covering everything from a SWAT callout on North Haynes Street to a pig who didn't want to leave an air conditioned police cruiser. No…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola Police Department PIO Mike Wood joined Pensacola Morning News Thursday — guest hosted by Greater Pensacola Chamber President Todd Thompson — with a wide-ranging update covering everything from a SWAT callout on North Haynes Street to a pig who didn't want to leave an air conditioned police cruiser.


No Name Apartments SWAT Callout

PPD's SWAT team and negotiators responded Friday afternoon to the No Name Apartments on North Haynes Street after a man threatening to harm himself was inside an apartment with a five-year-old child. Officers were able to get the child out safely first. The man eventually came out on his own and was taken to receive help without further incident. Wood used the moment to renew his warning about social media misinformation during active incidents — saying the same situation played out the week prior at Pensacola Village where someone posted online that ten people had been shot there, which was completely false. Wood says PPD's Facebook page has been significantly upgraded under Chief Winstrom to push accurate breaking news information quickly — and urged residents to rely on NewsRadio and PPD's official social media pages rather than keyboard warriors during breaking events.


Baptist Hospital Break-Ins — Still Happening, Still Getting Caught

Two juveniles and one adult were arrested Sunday night attempting to burglarize the old Baptist Hospital campus. Wood says PPD is now ten to twelve for zero on catching intruders at the site — with security cameras covering the entire campus during the active demolition. Wood says people — usually teenagers — keep trying to get in looking for copper wire, old furniture, or anything they can take. He says the chances of getting caught are approaching 100 percent and urges everyone to stay away from the campus entirely. He noted PPD is also undefeated at Blue Wahoos Stadium — another location with comprehensive camera coverage.


Back to School — School Zones and Bus Stops

With Escambia County students back in class this week Wood says PPD officers are actively watching school zones and bus stops. He says school zone speeding carries no warning — officers will write tickets because children's safety cannot be compromised. On bus stops he says the most common confusion point is four-lane roads — all traffic in both directions must stop when a bus extends its arm unless drivers would have to cross an unpaved grass median at least five feet wide to reach the bus. When in doubt slow down and stop. Wood says PPD has not seen a high volume of violations in the first week back but says enforcement is consistent and active.


Wilbert the Pig

The highlight of the week — PPD took a pig named Wilbert into temporary custody after he was spotted loose in East Pensacola Heights. An officer got Wilbert into the back of a cruiser where he apparently enjoyed the air conditioning quite a bit. Once his owners were identified and officers tried to return him home Wilbert refused to leave the cruiser. He was eventually lured out with double stuffed Oreo cookies and is back home doing well. Wood noted this was actually the third escaped pig PPD has dealt with this year — the first was on Garden Street, the second on Interstate 110, and now Wilbert in East Pensacola Heights. All three were different pigs. Wood says PPD may need to consider forming a dedicated escaped pig task force. He also noted that pigs are smart animals and putting one in air conditioning in August is a recipe for not getting them back out easily — which he says you really can't blame them for.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Former Century Mayor Luis Gomez Junior has died at 62. Gomez stepped into the role as interim mayor in 2023 after Ben Boutwell's resignation, later winning election unopposed twice before resigning himself in early 2025 for medical reasons. During his time in office, Gomez helped save the town nearly two-hundred-thousand dollars through insurance changes and outsourced management of the wastewater treatment plant. He was first elected to the town council back in 2017. Funeral arrangements have not yet been announced.

item.content:encoded:
Senator Richard Blumenthal is pressing the Navy for answers about conditions aboard the U-S-S Abraham Lincoln, now sailing toward its ninth month of an extended deployment in the Middle East. It comes after reports that multiple sailors attempted to go overboard amid concerns over water access, plumbing, and mental health support. The Navy disputes those specific claims, saying it hasn't identified an increase in reported suicidal thoughts or attempts, while acknowledging the strain of long deployments and some disruptions to mail and resupply. Blumenthal wants details on why the deployment keeps getting extended and how the Navy plans to sustain carrier presence in the region moving forward.

item.title: Community Health Northwest Florida Awarded $8.7 Million Rural Health Grant — $41 Million Coming to the Region
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Community Health Northwest Florida has landed an $8.7 million Rural Health Transformation Program grant — and as the lead applicant for a 15-organization regional coalition the organization will help manage more than $41.5 million flowing to Northwest Florida over the next five years. The award was announced…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Community Health Northwest Florida has landed an $8.7 million Rural Health Transformation Program grant — and as the lead applicant for a 15-organization regional coalition the organization will help manage more than $41.5 million flowing to Northwest Florida over the next five years.


The award was announced Tuesday by the Florida Agency for Health Care Administration and the federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services. It flows from a $50 billion federal Rural Health Transformation bill passed last year — with Florida receiving $209 million of that total to improve access to care in rural communities statewide. Year one funding for the full coalition is $16.1 million — with $3.99 million specifically allocated to Community Health Northwest Florida.


What It Means for Century and the Northern Region

The most immediate local impact will be felt in Century and the surrounding communities of northern Escambia County — an area that has long faced barriers to accessing routine health care. Community Health will expand its existing Industrial Boulevard clinic in Century to offer adult primary care and pediatric services. A second Century location will be reopened to provide women's health, behavioral health and psychiatry, and treatment for opioid use disorder. Both locations will also serve residents of nearby Jay in Santa Rosa County.


CEO Chandra Smiley says maternal health and infant mortality are among the first priorities for the northern region — areas where distance from care contributes directly to poor outcomes. She says getting patients access to preventive and chronic care management services closer to home keeps them out of emergency rooms and produces better long-term results at lower cost.


"This is truly a transformational opportunity for every rural patient in Northwest Florida," Smiley said. "We will be able to provide care closer to where our patients live and also help keep them out of emergency rooms. It will improve lives, save lives, and save money in the process."


The Coalition

Community Health Northwest Florida submitted the application on behalf of 15 partner organizations serving rural patients across the 10 westernmost counties in Florida. Partners include Sacred Heart, Bridgeway, Lakeview Services, Point Washington Medical Health and Hope, the Walton County Health Department's federally qualified health center arm, and others. The Northwest Florida Health Council — which supports regional health care access and education across Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa, and Walton Counties — will serve as the administrative oversight body for the grant. Community Health Northwest Florida will serve as the fiscal agent responsible for managing grant funds on behalf of all 15 organizations.


Smiley says the coalition approach was deliberate — pooling the collective reach and expertise of 15 organizations under one application to maximize the impact of available funding across the region.


More information is available at healthcarewithinreach.org or by calling Community Health Northwest Florida at 850-436-4630.

item.title: Governor DeSantis Announces $9 Million For New Boat Building Facilities At Port Of Pensacola
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Governor Ron DeSantis visited the Port of Pensacola Thursday to announce nine million dollars in state funding for two new boat building facilities, a move officials say will significantly expand the region's shipbuilding capacity and create thousands of jobs. The funding will support site development, utilities…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Governor Ron DeSantis visited the Port of Pensacola Thursday to announce nine million dollars in state funding for two new boat building facilities, a move officials say will significantly expand the region's shipbuilding capacity and create thousands of jobs.


The funding will support site development, utilities and construction of the two facilities, which together will add four-hundred-thousand square feet of manufacturing space at the port. DeSantis said the expansion will allow the facility to produce complex Navy ship modules for submarines and surface vessels up to four-hundred feet long.


"This is going to create approximately 2,000 manufacturing and related jobs in the shipbuilding and maritime manufacturing industry," DeSantis said, calling the investment a boost not just for the local economy, but for national defense.


DeSantis pointed to Florida's standing as the nation's top maritime state, home to 21 military installations and 16 deepwater seaports that together support nearly 20 billion dollars in gross domestic product and more than a million jobs statewide. He said Pensacola's location, workforce, and existing infrastructure made the port a natural fit for the expansion.


The announcement builds on a 3.9-million-dollar Job Growth Grant Fund award the state gave the City of Pensacola for port improvements back in 2023. DeSantis said those earlier upgrades helped establish the port as what he called a "high performance maritime center of excellence," work that also helped secure Pensacola's designation as home to America's High Performance Center, which opened earlier this year.


Thursday's investment comes alongside a separate 76-million-dollar grant from Triumph Gulf Coast, which DeSantis said will further strengthen the region's maritime industrial base.

"Today's investment... we're not only bolstering our maritime industry, but supporting national security and ensuring the United States remains a force in maritime dominance on the world stage," DeSantis said.


DeSantis, a former naval officer, said the moment carried personal significance given the region's deep ties to the U.S. Navy. City officials, including Mayor D.C. Reeves, joined DeSantis for the announcement.

item.title: Escambia County Early Voting Underway — Superintendent Referendum, School Board Races and Mayor's Race All on the Ballot
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Early voting is open right now in Escambia County for the August 18th primary election — and Supervisor of Elections Robert Bender says there is something on the ballot for every registered voter regardless of party affiliation. Early Voting Details Ten locations are open through Saturday from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Early voting is open right now in Escambia County for the August 18th primary election — and Supervisor of Elections Robert Bender says there is something on the ballot for every registered voter regardless of party affiliation.


Early Voting Details

Ten locations are open through Saturday from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Unlike election day voters can go to any early voting location — they do not need to go to their home precinct. Locations include Century Courthouse, Molino Community Center, the extension office on Stefani Road, Bellevue Lodge, Bellevue Library, UWF, Asbury Place near Ninth Avenue and College Boulevard, the downtown main library, the SOE office downtown, Brownsville Community Center, and the Southwest Library. Bender says 27 people voted in the first twelve minutes this morning and there are currently no lines at any location.


What's on the Ballot

Every Escambia County voter will see a countywide referendum on whether to make the school superintendent position appointed rather than elected — a significant policy question that has drawn considerable community attention. Three nonpartisan school board races for Districts 1, 2, and 3 are also on the ballot — with only two candidates in each race meaning the winner will be decided outright on August 18th without a November runoff.


The mayor's race features six candidates. Bender noted that four years ago Mayor Reeves received more than 50 percent of the vote in the August election and was elected outright without going to November. If any candidate clears 50 percent on August 18th there will be no November mayoral election.


Partisan races on the ballot include U.S. Senate, governor and lieutenant governor, CFO, and commissioner of agriculture — races that both Republicans and Democrats will see. Republicans also have a congressional race to replace termed-out Representative Alex Andrade and a county commission District 2 race. Bender says some ballots ran to a third column given the volume of races.


Governor and Lieutenant Governor — Only Pick One

Bender flagged an important note for voters on the governor and lieutenant governor race. The ballot lists it as a single contest, but most candidates have not yet selected a running mate — meaning only one name appears under each gubernatorial candidate. Voters should only select one candidate. On the Democratic side David Jolly is listed as lieutenant governor under Gwen Graham — voters should not be confused by seeing Gwen Graham's name without an oval next to it. If a voter accidentally selects two candidates in that contest the machine will flag it and give them an opportunity to fix it before the ballot is cast.


Mail-In Ballot Logistics

Voters who have a mail-in ballot but have not yet returned it can drop it at any early voting location during open hours using the secure ballot intake station. On election day the only drop-off location is the SOE office downtown — precincts do not accept mail-in ballot drop-offs on election day. A voter who shows up at their precinct on election day with a mail-in ballot can surrender it and vote in person instead. All mail-in ballots must be in Bender's possession by 7 p.m. on election night to be counted. Voters can now track their ballot through the USPS system — and can check their ballot status at escambiavotes.gov under the voters tab.


Citizenship and Name Questions

Bender addressed social media concerns about married name mismatches and citizenship verification at the polls. He says voters should not be concerned — photo ID matching the name on the voter record is all that is required for 2026. Citizenship verification requirements for new voters do not take effect until 2027. Existing voters whose citizenship was verified when they registered remain on the rolls without any additional documentation needed.


New I Voted Sticker

This year's I Voted sticker features a commemorative America 250 design — a tall ship representing 1776 and an American Magic-style sailing vessel representing 2026 with fireworks faded in the background. The sticker is slightly larger than previous years. Mail-in ballot packets also include the sticker along with a yellow-highlighted signature area on the return envelope designed to reduce signature errors and help postal workers identify ballots quickly.


Election day is August 18th from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. — voters must go to their home precinct. Questions can be directed to the Supervisor of Elections office at 850-595-3900 or escambiavotes.gov.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County Library Director Christal Bell-Rivera has resigned, effective September ninth, with no explanation given. Bell-Rivera's hiring in March drew controversy after County Administrator Wes Moreno appointed her over two higher-ranked candidates recommended by the West Florida Library Board. At the time, she didn't yet meet minimum qualifications for the role, though she has since completed her master's degree in library science. She had served as interim director since Todd Humble's retirement last November.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County Schools Superintendent Keith Leonard says Booker T. Washington High School's HVAC overhaul is still underway as students return to class Wednesday - and says some disruption is expected to continue into the first semester before the project wraps up.


"That's about an 18-month project, " Leonard told Jennifer Harrison on Pensacola's Morning News on Monday. "Last year... I was having to move students from one wing to another wing while we were doing that project. They were really steadfast and overcame a bunch of obstacles."


Leonard says students may continue to work around the work for the first semester this year. He says the district has been working on the project all summer and says students and staff at Booker T. have shown great flexibility throughout. Classes resume for all 31,000 Escambia County students this Wednesday.

Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County commissioners honored two employees at last night's meeting. Sheila Knight, a custodial worker who has served the county for more than 33 years, was recognized for her retirement, with commissioners and coworkers praising her dedication and positive impact on everyone she's worked with over the decades. Commissioner Lumon May offered personal remarks, crediting Knight's advice and support as part of what inspired him to run for office. Separately, commissioners recognized Robert Carlin, the county's Information Security Officer, as Employee of the Month for August. item.title: One Energy Place Sells to Local Investors, Reopens as Multi-Tenant Office Building
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- One of the most recognizable buildings on the Pensacola waterfront has a new owner — and for the first time in four decades it is opening its doors to more than one tenant. The sale of One Energy Place at 500 Bayfront Parkway closed July 31st — transitioning the iconic five-story 250,000 square foot building from…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- One of the most recognizable buildings on the Pensacola waterfront has a new owner — and for the first time in four decades it is opening its doors to more than one tenant.


The sale of One Energy Place at 500 Bayfront Parkway closed July 31st — transitioning the iconic five-story 250,000 square foot building from FPL's single-tenant Northwest Florida headquarters to a multi-tenant Class A office property under new local ownership. The deal was brokered by Michael Carro, Managing Director of SVN Southland Commercial, who represented both the seller and brought the buyer to the table after six years of working with FPL on the property's valuation.


For the community the most significant detail may be the simplest one — the building is staying local. "One Energy Place has anchored the Pensacola bayfront for nearly forty years and it means a great deal that this landmark will remain in local hands," Carro said. "Converting it from a single corporate headquarters into a multi-tenant Class A building opens the door for a range of local and regional businesses to call the waterfront home."


The building was constructed in 1986 as the corporate headquarters of Gulf Power — which had served Northwest Florida since 1926. When Gulf Power merged into Florida Power and Light in 2021 and the Gulf Power name was retired in 2022 the building continued as FPL's Northwest Florida headquarters until being brought to market. Under the new arrangement FPL is staying on the campus as one of the building's tenants.


Leasing activity ahead of the closing was strong. By the time the sale closed 127,000 of the building's 250,000 square feet had already been committed — and Carro says active negotiations on an additional 100,000 square feet are continuing with multiple prospective tenants.


"The reception for this property has been overwhelmingly positive with a lot of leases getting inked prior to closing and a lot of paper continuing to trade hands as we speak," Carro said.

The building sits on 13.38 acres of prime waterfront real estate — fronting not just Bayfront Parkway but extending all the way to Chase Street. Carro says the new ownership group sees future development potential on the site tied to technology and innovation — with a possible connection to what is happening at the Bayfront auditorium.


One feature generating particular interest is a restaurant space with sweeping water views of Pensacola Bay. The dining room was once home to Norman's — a landmark Pensacola restaurant that longtime residents remember fondly. Carro says he is actively looking for a restaurateur ready to bring it back to life.


"If we can find a restaurant operator that wants to come in — please have them give me a call," Carro said.


The building is now being marketed for lease as new ownership takes possession. Leasing inquiries can be directed to Michael Carro at SVN Southland Commercial — 850-434-7500 or mcarro@svn.com.
